claims.claim: TSMC has suspended Chinese chip-design orders at 16 nanometres and below unless the customer obtains a US export licence, and generally limits those customers to 28 nm and 40 nm without HBM or advanced packaging.
claims.episode_span: orders at 16 nanometres and below are suspended unless a US export licence is in hand
claims.source_title: TSMC Tightens China Chip Restrictions Following New US Export Rules
claims.supporting_quote: The world’s largest contract chipmaker has instructed that orders involving manufacturing processes of 16 nanometres and below be suspended unless customers obtain US export licences, the sources said.

claims.claim: The US Commerce Department rules took effect Thursday after being set by the Bureau of Industry and Security on November 16, and Samsung as well as TSMC suspended some shipments to Chinese customers while seeking licences.
claims.episode_span: The Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security set the restrictions on November 16; they took effect Thursday, November 19
claims.source_title: U.S. Tightens AI Chip Export Controls... Samsung Electronics, TSMC Halt Chip Shipments to Chinese Customers
claims.supporting_quote: On November 16, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS), which is part of the U.S. Department of Commerce, said that companies using U.S. technology to produce advanced semiconductors must obtain export licenses to sell products ultimately destined for Chinese customers.

claims.claim: A US approved-designer list includes Nvidia, AMD, Apple, MediaTek and Realtek and no mainland Chinese companies, and TSMC will scrutinize locations, parents, shareholders, packaging providers and shipping routes including overseas intermediaries.

claims.supporting_quote: Mainland Chinese firms are absent from a US government roster of authorised designers, which includes Apple Inc, MediaTek Inc, Nvidia, Realtek Semiconductor Corp and Advanced Micro Devices Inc.
